body: scripts/stack carries no @decision/@story annotations, though the notes' Changes entry lists them at their sites: checks/materialized-standalone lints each payload script in a repo with no citation config, so any `# @decision:` line fails it (comment-hygiene), and the payload's scripts carry none (the closed-issues call: 'Materialized scripts carry no annotations'). The annotations (decision:stack-tool-runs-each-run, run-artifacts-recorded-by-the-stack-tool, run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run, per-run-artifact-tag, ports-leased-from-a-project-range, story:verification-leaves-no-artifacts-behind, story:concurrent-stacks-without-port-collisions) belong on the scripts/stack row of admin/true-up::EXECUTABLE_FILES, which the stack-trueup stage adds.

A stack.json entry records `tag_variable` beside at/ports/folder/declared/stop/holder/refused/stopping, so down and cleanup rebuild the start environment the run started with (coding rule 3.3), as `stop` is recorded.

Event kinds beyond the four the notes list, one per catch the events standard requires to emit: STACK.REMOVAL.REFUSED (a stop/group/docker/folder step a down or cleanup records as refused), STACK.GROUP.GONE (killpg found the group already gone), STACK.CLEANUP.UNCHECKED (cleanup could not list a run's running containers, so it leaves the run).

`stack up -- <command> ...` runs that argv directly (no sh -c) from the project root, with stdin /dev/null and output to <folder>/stack-start.log as the declared start does; a program not runnable from the root (not on PATH, or a relative path not executable from the root) is refused before any lease. `up --` with an unfilled declaration still opens a run (no tag variable set); a malformed declaration refuses `up` with or without `--`.

scripts/plumbline::configDefects now passes the whole config as a third argument to every CONFIG_KEY_DEFECTS validator, so stackDefects(value, repoRoot, userConfig) checks the port names against tag_variable, OK_RUN_LABEL, OK_RUN_FOLDER, and COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME; the other validators ignore the argument. That port check runs only where `stack` is declared, in plumbline and in scripts/stack alike.

stackDefects and scripts/stack::stack_defects refuse two shapes beyond the notes' list: a stack setting neither start nor none, and stop without start. The two tools print the same defect texts; scripts/stack names all of them in one refusal and names config-check.

scripts/stack::declared_stack(config) returns (state, reason): ('stack', the start command), ('none', the stack.none text), or ('unfilled', a message naming stack.start with stack.tag_variable, or stack.none, in .ok-planner/config.json); it raises stack.Refusal on a malformed declaration or malformed ports. The review stage reads state from element 0.

down prints `took down: <tag> (<ports>; <n> container(s), <n> network(s), <n> volume(s), <n> image(s))` on success, the same line cleanup prints. list prints each run's ports in name order, as stack.json stores them with sorted keys, while up prints them in declared order.

A run's recorded stop command is the one down runs for its life: where it always fails (as a stop that tests a file in the deleted run folder would), every later down and cleanup records the refusal and keeps the entry, and only a fixed command in a fresh run avoids it. Recording stop at up follows the notes and coding rule 3.3.
Process-group membership excludes zombies (ps stat Z), and up reaps its own holder child after signalling the group on a failed or interrupted start, so the group reads empty once its members exit.

Docker on PATH with its daemon unreachable (Docker Desktop stopped): down's label removals fail, so down records the refusal, keeps the entry and lease, and exits 1, and cleanup leaves the run with the reason until the daemon answers. Options: (a) built: a removal docker cannot answer is refused, since down cannot show the run's labelled objects are gone; (b) treat an unreachable daemon as docker absent, so the run's entry is deleted and any labelled images, volumes, or networks it made stay on disk unrecorded.

body: scripts/plumbline: composeServiceBlocks(lines, section = 'services') takes the top-level section it walks, so checkComposeLabels walks services, volumes, and networks with the one iterator (coding rule 6); composePortEntries and portsKeyEntries/flowEntry now share it and three small helpers factored from them (untagged, childBlock, flowItems). compose-ports subcommand output and compose-ports violations diffed identical before and after on throwaway compose files.

compose-labels accepts a labels sequence item only where the whole item is the variable: ${OK_RUN_LABEL}, ${OK_RUN_LABEL:-x}, ${OK_RUN_LABEL-x}, or $OK_RUN_LABEL. An item such as ok.run-tag=${OK_RUN_LABEL} reports, since OK_RUN_LABEL already holds ok.run-tag=<tag>. Flow ([..]) and block sequences both count; map-form labels (block or {..}) report as rule map-labels; a scalar labels value reports as missing.

compose-labels default network: where top-level networks.default is declared without the label, the check reports it once at that declaration (as it reports every named network) and not again on the first attaching service; where it is declared external, nothing reports. A top-level volume or network counts as external where external is true or the legacy mapping form (external: {name: x} or a nested block). Violation rule ids, read by patternKey as compose-labels:<rule>: service, build, build-scalar, map-labels, volume, network, default-network.

body: admin/retired-boilerplate.json and checks/sprint-boilerplate read every v* tag, v5-v7 included: v5-v6 held the template at plugins/ok-planner/skills/sprint/SKILL.md and v7 at plugins/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md (Completion contract only), so the check reads five homes, not the Call's four, per the work item's 'whatever release laid it out'. In every home a section is bounded to the template's markdown fence (the one after '### {{SPRINT-DOCUMENT-TEMPLATE}}' where the file has that heading, the first column-0 ```markdown fence otherwise). The set holds 816 lines; every line the removed RETIRED_CONTRACT_ITEM, retire_contract_item renumbering, 3-space RETIRED_PATH_LINES, and RETIRED_DRAIN_STEPS rewrote is in it (checked).

checks/sprint-boilerplate takes no inputs, as its sibling checks do, and has no write mode: where the carried template changes, a maintainer edits admin/retired-boilerplate.json by the lines the check's failure names (missing, carried, or never released, plus an order check). The check re-derives the section bounds itself rather than importing them: the core's are inside the bash heredoc of admin/true-up and cannot be imported, and the check exists to verify the payload's data independently.

admin/true-up::section_bounds sets a section's trailing blank lines aside before matching and keeps them, so a sprint's file ending is unchanged (a final-newline loss otherwise when a retired last line sits at end of file); inside a replaced hunk a blank line counts as a template line, so the carried side supplies the hunk's spacing. A section's end is the next '## ' line or column-0 fence, or end of file.
